summary: Tested Issues module (customer_complaints) multi-user/multi-department, close/reopen, no-category, IdleBadge, XLSX import/export. Backend 5/6 pytest pass; frontend desktop + mobile E2E passed end-to-end (create with 2 depts + 2 assignees, list badges, close→reopen, delete, legacy issue detail).

minor.issue: Existing issue CMP-2026-0001 'Leaking bottle cap' has empty departments=[] and assignees=[] arrays. Review request stated it should show departments=['Production'] after migration. Either the migration never ran, or the source doc had no legacy 'department'/'assigned_to' populated. Both list row and detail Manage panel now display 'No departments' / 'Unassigned' for this issue.

verified_flows: POST /api/complaints with departments+assignees arrays returns arrays and mirrors legacy assigned_to/assigned_to_name/department (first entry)
PUT departments/assignees updates and re-mirrors legacy fields
PUT status='closed' sets closed_at; PUT status='open' from closed sets reopened_at
GET /api/complaints?assigned_to=<id> matches assignees.id; ?assigned_to=unassigned returns empty-assignee docs
GET /api/complaints/export xlsx headers include 'Departments' and 'Assignees', no 'Category'
POST /api/complaints/import with Departments='Production, Quality' and Assignees='Alice, Bob' correctly parses both arrays
Frontend /complaints list: no Category filter, no 'Group by Category', table has Departments (badges), Assignees (comma-joined), Last Update column with data-testid idle-badge-{id}
New Issue dialog: no Category select; complaint-departments-select multi-select works (Production+Quality); complaint-assignees-select multi-select works (Amit Chopra, Cathy Director)
Created issue appears in list with both dept badges + both assignee names + 'Updated today'
Detail header shows priority/status badges, dept badges, 'Updated today' idle badge
complaint-close-btn → status Closed → button becomes complaint-reopen-btn → click reopens back to Open (button flips back to Close)
Delete via detail 'Delete' → confirm-delete-complaint removes issue and navigates back to list
Legacy issue CMP-2026-0001 loads on detail with inline-edit pencils present
Mobile 390x844: complaints-card-list renders with idle-badge inside each card
action_items: Investigate why CMP-2026-0001 has empty departments/assignees arrays. Confirm migration script actually ran on production and copies legacy 'department' → 'departments=[department]' and legacy 'assigned_to*' → 'assignees=[{id,name}]'. If it did run but the source doc had no legacy dept, expected behavior — otherwise re-run migration.
critical_code_review_comments: customer_complaints.py:539 — status_raw fallback logic is fine but the 'in_progress' normalisation is only applied if the raw value already exists in STATUSES; low priority.
Import endpoint does not enforce a per-file row cap; a maliciously large xlsx could DOS. Consider cap of ~5000 rows.
Assignee ids in import are always None (no user lookup by name). This means legacy assigned_to filter by id won't work for imported rows — only by name via search.
seed_data_creation: Created E2E test issue CMP-2026-0002; deleted at end. Import test created a TEST_import_multi_v2 row; deleted at end.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_complaints_multi_v2.py. Only outstanding item is the migration state of CMP-2026-0001 (see backend_issues.minor).
rca of the issue: CMP-2026-0001 shows empty departments/assignees. Likely the migration script that was supposed to copy legacy scalar fields into arrays either did not run or the source doc had null legacy fields to begin with. Reproduce: GET /api/complaints?search=CMP-2026-0001 → returns doc with departments=[] department=null assignees=[] assigned_to_name=null. Mitigation: re-run migration copying doc.department into doc.departments (if not empty) and building assignees=[{id:assigned_to, name:assigned_to_name}] when legacy fields are set.
